correctness.rationale: A direct centered Rayleigh witness bounds the spectral gap above the sharp price. The parabolic path weights saturate it and the entire path Laplacian spectrum is verified analytically through invariant polynomial subspaces. At price equality, the eigenvector equations force a one-dimensional affine allocation family; positivity on the orthogonal complement gives an exact positive generalized-Rayleigh endpoint. When price decreases, rescaling a positive-bridge equality optimizer gives strictly greater gap, so a deleted bridge cannot be optimal. The n=5 root is obtained by direct characteristic-polynomial factorization. The extracted standalone checker succeeded with 178 exact symbolic/rational checks; finite tests are supplementary.

originality.rationale: Result 5 of Sun et al. already solves weighted paths and the four-cycle one-defect case was recorded separately; neither is claimed as new. Their Section 5.3 gives the unpriced cycle and a two-dimensional eigenvalue-multiplicity bound, not the sharp single-defect cost threshold across all cycles with at least five vertices and its full critical optimizer interval. A 2012 Laplacian-weight design paper presents a general spectral feasibility algorithm, not that explicit structural classification. Searches of published-result records and accessible related statements found no stronger implication with the same price, cycle-size and optimizer-face scope. This supports qualified originality, not a proof of unique publication priority.
residual_risks: Older unindexed weighted-cycle edge-deletion or maximum-variance duality results could imply part or all of the claim.
Full text of Fiedler (1993) was not accessible; possible broader coverage cannot be excluded by its abstract.
A general SDP solver can produce these designs but is not itself an explicit published phase classification. Independent priority and mathematical review remain needed.

value.rationale: A sharply priced link in a cycle is a canonical network screening decision; the exact squared-path-length cutoff applies at every network size n>=5. The nonunique optimal allocation segment at the threshold is a structural spectral-design phenomenon, and its finite generalized eigenvalue endpoint is computable; the first five-cycle endpoint is a new closed radical. Unlike restating an SDP, the result identifies all boundary optimizers and proves that below the cutoff every optimum must fund the closing edge.
